items.note: Story 1: Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association, 1889 at Larrow Green, Gideon Vose first president, creamery 1891.
Story 1: paid on pounds of butterfat by test, not weight; test at the station where he delivered set his pay.

Section A only calls Article VII 'the hinge of everything later'. The weight-vs-test point ('under payment by weight nobody would have lost a dollar') appears only in B3 and F1, and credit cannot travel into A.
Only Teague is named as bookkeeper. Effie Loomis as secretary and Hobart Sill as buttermaker are absent, so the core of the list is missing.
Selby Vose is named as the founder's son but made manager 'from 1911'. The key says 1913.
Story 5 (headed 1898-1925): yearly 'station gain ... five and a quarter per cent, as usual, carried to the general account', i.e. more fat arrived than was credited.
Story 1: Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up, built winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, borrowed Larrow Green glass.

Covered: weighed, sampled, tested, cream to Larrow Green, skim returned, and the short charge in a bottle ruled for a full charge. Composite sample not named, but the core fact is present (list-type item).
Story 2: Ammon & Sons, Tarnet, invoice 14 April 1897, in use 1 May 1897.
Story 2 gives the full invoice: 6 doz pipettes 17.6 c.c., 12 doz bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
Story 3: short by 0.19 in every month, June flush and February alike; steadiness is the mark of an instrument error.
Never says a pipette cannot be checked without a burette or that the county had none.
Ansel Keddie 1861-1934, twenty-nine seasons 1896-1924 (story 1); dismissed 30 April 1925 (story 7).
Gating element present: the station test book in Keddie's hand, where he recorded every figure. Columns and initialed corrections (context) are absent.
Summary leaf never reported. No 1896 recorded average of 3.80 against 3.61 from 1898. The run's 3.80 is only the derived true average.
Story 4: nine weeks, broken 8 May, borrowed measure to 10 July, tests higher, back to old level, question mark. The 3.80 figure is missing (run says it has none), but the core event is intact.
Married Orra Brant, sister of Emmet Brant, the largest patron.
The 1919 circular is present, but Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement (tested as taught, cannot say why) is absent. Both are required.
Died February 1934 'after nine years under the charge'; test book impounded 1925, to the Historical Rooms 1959.
Hessel Bottom, six farms, Emmet Brant's the largest.
Weigh book begun 1 January 1897; the two scales agreed.
1902 complaints present. The gaps are kept apart: Larrow Green 3.78 vs 3.61, and the true shortfall 0.19 from 3.80. Hollow-vs-Green is never called 0.19.
The committee came up in January and reported in March 1908, but the Jan-Mar sampling window is not stated and Grigg appears only as the sleigh owner.
200,000 lb on 3.42; the gap of 0.18 is exactly 5%, a proportional error.
Story 8: weigh book borrowed from Roy Brant in 1958, then Roy to Hazel.
Cudd's factory at Alder Corners 'over the ridge'. Redlow Ridge is never named and Vessey County is not given as the factory's county.
Four of the six Bottom farms hauled their summer-flush milk over the ridge. The 1915 start is missing, but the core fact is present.
'Same cows and hay, different glass' (other glassware) plus the named artifact ('the Alder Corners test figures', 'the Cudd book'): two of four elements, framed as a control.
The same four farms' milk tested 0.19 higher at Alder Corners. Sixteen seasons is not stated.
'The same milk tested 0.19 higher: same cows and hay, different glass'.
Rosalie Cudd, Jerome's daughter, copied the Alder Corners figures for Ivy in 1958.
Strawn is named, but his work is dated 'from 1908' (NT-23). The key says 1907-1936.
Lactometer at every visit, never found added water.
12 June 1923, calibrated burette, whole lot condemned.
Recorded the condemnation but nothing about what the glass had been doing for 26 years.
Gives the 1924 average as 3.85, not 3.80. A wrong 1924 average loses the item.
Crate to the loft; notebooks to the state dairy office, then the Farland library in 1947.
Petition January 1925.
Board sat 17 March - 4 May 1925, three sittings, two in the station weigh room. Chairman Frick not named (only 'an Ashlin attorney'); core fact present.
Three theories argued (water, tester skimming, wet hay); board found no cause established.
Four books listed including Strawn's condemnation-year notebook; nobody set it beside the test book.
Dismissed 30 April 1925, four days before the finding; 4 May $3,800 without admission, charged to the station account.
One-fifth of $19,000 is stated, but the award is never tied to the account where the loss had built up as 'gain'. The gain is said to go to the 'general account'.
Ivy Keddie b. 1931, Ansel's granddaughter, dairy husbandry at Farland, Prof. Leland Vaught.
'Gathered records that no one had put together': weigh book, Strawn notebook, Alder Corners figures.
Feb 1958 crate in the loft is present, but the run declares nine vs eleven unsettleable and never states nine survived.
9 March 1958, burette, 16.72 against 17.6 (95%); 0.88 c.c. short in story 2.
40,000,000 lb; 76,000 lb; $19,000 at 25c; the 76,000 lb gain is the ledger's station-gain line ('the missing butterfat, recorded in ink').
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958; 33 years after the dismissal, 24 after the death; crate in the loft thirty-five years.
Granddaughter.
Ivy is Duncan's daughter; Duncan is Ansel's son.
Second cousins via Emmet/Orra siblings, Roy/Duncan first cousins.
Says full vs half siblings cannot be settled (pre-1889 pages lost). No assertion. Wrongly adds that half-siblings would make them 'half second cousins', but that clause is unbolded context.
Gideon Vose, father; nephew rejected.
Father's Article VII made the test decide pay; the son ran the father's system and blamed the patrons.
Headline: 'No relationship is established, and the better evidence is that there was none.' E#7 marks it 'Resolved: no relation shown'. Never declares the question unsettleable.
Treats the family denial as outranking the hearsay, which contradicts the key (a family member's denial is not a record). No statement that no document names or denies a link.
$90 = 360 x $0.25, explicitly using the long-run average because the 1910 price was not in its sources. Meets the key's stated acceptance condition.
76,000 lb = 5.26% of fat credited, 5.00% of fat actually received; denominators named.
$77.93 with the line items.
72 pipettes, 0.88 c.c. short each.
26 years 1 month 11 days; 25 full years 1898-1922; part years excluded.
Cannot be determined; Kyle's figure is hearsay.
Variable: the station's measuring glass (its own measure broke, borrowed one used).
Tester, herds, pasture, season, separator, scales, acid held constant.
Result given only as 'rose markedly' and 'fell back'. The 3.80 and 3.61 figures are missing (run says it has none).
Cause lies in the glass, not man/cows/hay, and it cuts against theft. Limits: size of error, which item was faulty.
1911 interval (r22/r24), ledger surplus (r23), post-1923 rise (r22), Alder Corners (r17): three narrators.
Independence argued; says reasons 1-3 hold without the 1958 measurement.
A09 asserted: 'Did the bookkeeper question the entries? No.'
Yes, he knew the tests ran low: 1919 circular, complaints since 1902.

Only two of five are valid: signed the ledger with the gain line, and the 1919 circular. Manager date given as 1911 (wrong); watering at the 1925 hearing and 'nothing in his hand names the glassware' are absent.
A03 asserted: 'he did not know why'; 'he knew the tests were low and blamed the patrons... none that he suspected the glass'. No declared inability.

Resolved with method: weigh book 1897 vs 1900 (custody list); Orra 1866 vs 1868 (r18's own 'eighty-two in 1948'); 1908 committee vs 1925 board as two bodies; Keddie start 1896 vs 'ninety-five'. Note: circular reach resolved the wrong way (eleven).
NT-14 ($77.39 in r19 and r20's prose, broken by the line items) and NT-18 (great-niece in r19 and r22, broken by r18 and r22's correction). No third valid pair.
A04: cannot be settled, works books burned 1931. A06 not addressed as a conflict. A10 is abstained only in Section A story 1, which the B-G scope rule excludes.
r18 1868 vs 'eighty-two in 1948'; r20 'nothing before 1900' vs its 1897 invoice.

72 pipettes, 16.72 vs 17.6, 0.95 x true; 0.19 = 5% of 3.80, 0.18 on Emmet's 3.60; onset 1 May 1897, end June-July 1923, nothing else changed. Contains the wrong 3.85 post-1923 average (deducted separately); the gating elements are present.
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer and Brant's agreeing scales.
Theft defeated by the ledger surplus (cream arrived heavy), the 1911 interval and the rise under the same man.
Bog hay defeated by Bulletin 214 (0.05 winter, nothing summer) and Alder Corners.
A07 asserted: 'Did the 1925 board examine the condemned glass? No.'
A05 asserted: 'What did the tester believe? From 1911, the glass.'
About 138 words.
Invoice, weigh book, ledger, Strawn notebook, rival factory's tests, 1958 measurement: at least five.
No decoy stated as fact; no wrong headline figure.
5% short, 1897, 76,000 lb/$19,000, 1923, 1958, Ansel and Ivy Keddie.

deductions.reason: Corruption: Selby Vose manager from 1911 asserted (story 5, story 4, B3, D3)
Corruption: Strawn's circuit/lactometer visits from 1908 asserted (story 5, F2) - NT-23
Corruption: 1924 average of 3.85 asserted (story 6, C1b, D2, F1, F3)
Corruption: circular sent to eleven families asserted (story 5, E#20)
Gullibility A01: Vose-Keddie kinship 'resolved' as no relation (B4 headline lean, E#7 'Resolved')
Gullibility A09: bookkeeper never questioned the entries asserted (D2)
Gullibility A03: manager's knowledge of the understatement answered (D3: 'did not know why', 'none that he suspected the glass')
Gullibility A07: board did not examine the glass asserted (F)
Gullibility A05: tester believed it was the glass asserted (F)
